global_cases.case_name: Kyrgyzstan Digital Som CBDC (In Progress — Law Enacted 2025)
global_cases.problem_solved: KG has high remittance dependency ($3B+/year, 25% of GDP) with expensive and slow cross-border transfers via Western Union/MoneyGram, and significant unbanked rural population (45% of adults). Digital som (CBDC) could reduce remittance cost, provide government transfer efficiency for pensions/social payments, and extend financial inclusion to rural populations with only mobile phone access.
global_cases.architecture_summary: NBKR design in progress (as of May 2026): two-tier CBDC — NBKR issues digital som, commercial banks and licensed payment operators distribute wallets to consumers. Technical design: blockchain or distributed ledger for settlement (specific technology TBD based on BIS/IMF advisory). Wallet types: full KYC (higher limits), simplified KYC (lower limits), offline-capable wallet for rural areas. Programmable payments: conditioned transfers for social benefits. Cross-border: proposed integration with KZ digital tenge (when available) and EAEU payment rails. Legal basis: Law on CBDC amendments to National Bank Law (April 2025) and USDKG stablecoin law (2025). Full CBDC in force: planned January 2027.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: LAW ENACTED — implementation in progress. NBKR pilot announced Q3 2026. Target: 500,000 wallets in first year. Government ambition: replace current paper-based social transfer system with digital som payments by 2028.
global_cases.failure_modes: Technology choice risk: premature blockchain commitment may not be optimal for KG's transaction volumes. Rural offline wallet complexity. Banking sector lobbying to slow implementation. USDKG stablecoin (separate product) created regulatory confusion with digital som. Cybersecurity: CBDC is a critical infrastructure target.
global_cases.replicability_factors: This IS a KG case — provided as the active benchmark for what NBKR is building. Key: the procurement opportunity is the WALLET INFRASTRUCTURE — the technical platform for issuing, managing, and transacting digital som. The law is signed; the technology vendor is not yet selected.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ CBU is monitoring KG digital som as a nearby precedent. If KG's CBDC succeeds, UZ will face political pressure to implement equivalent. Lessons from KG digital som design will directly inform UZ CBU's future CBDC architecture. Score 7: UZ is 2-3 years behind KG in CBDC trajectory.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: This IS the KG case — it is in procurement. The wallet vendor selection ($5-10M for core infrastructure), government transfer integration ($3-5M), and cross-border remittance API ($2-3M) are all active opportunities in 2026-2027 window.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: N/A — this is the KG case itself. Key decisions pending: (1) blockchain vs conventional distributed database; (2) BIS CBDC reference implementation (mBridge) vs custom; (3) wallet UI/UX vendor; (4) social payment integration with MFSD (Ministry of Finance and Social Development).

global_cases.case_name: Singapore SPF i-Witness Crime Reporting & Analytics
global_cases.problem_solved: Singapore Police Force (SPF) needed to modernise evidence submission (citizens submitting photos/videos of incidents), reduce police workload from trivial reports, and improve crime pattern analysis. Digital evidence from citizens was arriving via email and WhatsApp in unstructured formats that overwhelmed analyst capacity.
global_cases.architecture_summary: i-Witness digital platform: citizen-facing web/app for crime reporting with structured input forms, geolocation tagging, and digital evidence upload (photos, video, screenshots). AI backend: image and video content analysis (detecting relevant vs irrelevant evidence uploads), report classification (crime type tagger), duplicate report detection, crime heat map generation for patrol resource allocation. SPF Command Centre: real-time dashboard showing incident clusters, resource allocation recommendations. Integration with SPF case management system. NLP: automated routing of written reports to correct investigative unit.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 35% increase in crime report submissions (digital friction reduced). Analyst workload per report: 40% reduction. Crime pattern identification: 2 major syndicated crime networks identified via digital evidence clustering. False report rate: 8% identified and diverted before officer response. Patrol deployment optimisation: 15% improvement in response times.
global_cases.failure_modes: Evidence admissibility: AI-processed digital evidence requires authentication chain for court use. Privacy concerns about AI analysis of uploaded videos. Some citizens submit low-quality evidence (blurry photos) that AI cannot process — still requires human triage. System targeted by malicious evidence uploads to overwhelm processing.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Architecture is standard citizen-reporting platform + AI triage. Applicable to any urban police force with smartphone-penetrant population. Donor pathway: UN Crime Prevention and Justice programme, UNODC.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ MIA (Ministry of Internal Affairs) has citizen-reporting portals but lacks AI analytics layer. Crime pattern analysis and patrol optimisation have government support. Key concern: AI analytics must not embed racial or socioeconomic profiling. Budget: $3-6M for UZ crime reporting AI upgrade. Sensitive politically — avoid predictive policing features.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG police have a citizens' complaint portal. AI triage to reduce officer workload is valuable in a police force facing budget constraints. The patrol optimisation module is highest-value for Bishkek. Budget: $2-4M. Donor pathway: OSCE, UNODC, UNDP rule-of-law programmes in KG.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language reporting interface. Avoid predictive/pre-crime features — focus on reported crime response optimisation only. Court-admissible digital evidence chain documentation. GDPR-equivalent data handling for uploaded images.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan eGümrük Digital Customs & Border AI
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan's border checkpoints processed 1.5M+ cargo entries annually with manual customs declaration review that averaged 2-3 day clearance times, 30% of cargo physically inspected (unsustainable), and significant corruption at customs windows. The State Revenue Committee needed AI risk-scoring to focus inspections on high-risk cargo while fast-tracking compliant operators.
global_cases.architecture_summary: eGümrük platform (Committee of State Revenue, KRS): digital customs declaration (e-CD) submitted online; AI risk scoring engine evaluating 50+ parameters (commodity, origin, importer history, route, price anomaly); Green/Yellow/Red channel assignment; automatic fast-track for trusted traders (Green channel: no inspection, 2-hour clearance). ASTANA-1 electronic scanner integration: X-ray scanners feed images to AI image analysis for contraband detection. Integration with EAEU Common Customs Information Space (shared data with Russia, Belarus, Armenia). Mobile app for customs declarations at small border crossings.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Customs clearance average: 48 hours to 8 hours (Green channel: under 2 hours). Physical inspection rate: reduced from 30% to 8% (AI risk-scoring focusing inspections). Customs revenue: +18% over 3 years (reduced corruption and under-declaration detection). Contraband detection rate at X-ray: improved 25% with AI image analysis. EAEU compliance: Kazakhstan ranked #1 in EAEU for customs digitalisation.
global_cases.failure_modes: Nuctech scanner controversy: EU has restricted Nuctech equipment on security grounds — creates geopolitical sensitivity for CA partners with Western donors. EAEU data sharing limitations: Russia delayed full data sharing for 3 years. AI risk scoring is opaque — traders cannot see why they received Red channel, limiting appeals.
global_cases.replicability_factors: eGümrük architecture is documented in EAEU customs harmonisation reports. CIS customs cooperation platform shares reference architecture. WCO (World Customs Organisation) has published guidance using KZ as reference. Directly applicable to UZ GTK (State Customs Committee) and KG GTS.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ GTK has deployed e-customs declaration but lacks the AI risk scoring layer. This is one of the highest-ROI applications in the entire tournament: UZ customs revenue leakage estimated at $500M-1B/year. Kazakhstan's $45M investment returned $180M+ in additional revenue in Year 1. KRS advisory available. EAEU common customs information space includes UZ aspirationally. Budget: $10-20M for UZ AI customs risk scoring. World Bank, ADB trade facilitation projects are donor pathways.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG is a significant transit country on the Bishkek-Osh-China route. Customs AI risk scoring would address documented transit fraud (goods declared as transit but sold domestically). Budget: $5-10M. Donor pathway: World Bank trade facilitation, EU DigiConnect4CA (digital connectivity for CA). KRS advisory is available.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language customs declaration interface. Avoid Nuctech scanners if EU donor funding involved (procurement restriction risk). EAEU data sharing integration for both UZ and KG. Trader appeal mechanism for AI Red channel assignment (rule-of-law requirement).

global_cases.case_name: Estonia National Cyber Defence Centre (NCSC & CERT-EE)
global_cases.problem_solved: Estonia's 2007 cyberattack (DDoS on Estonian government and banking systems — attributed to Russian state actors) exposed critical infrastructure vulnerabilities and demonstrated that e-government is only as strong as its cybersecurity. Estonia built a comprehensive national cyber defence architecture to protect digital government services.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Three-pillar architecture: (1) CERT-EE (Computer Emergency Response Team) — 24/7 incident response, threat intelligence sharing with EU/NATO partners, national vulnerability disclosure programme; (2) NCSC-EE (National Cyber Security Centre) — policy, standards, cybersecurity requirements for critical infrastructure; (3) Cyber Command (military) — national defence cyber capabilities. Key technical innovations: government network monitoring (ISKE baseline security framework for all government systems), national backup data embassies (copies of X-Road + land registry stored in Luxembourg and UK), cybersecurity exercise programme (Cyber Range at TalTech). Annual CyCon (Cyber Conference) hosted by NATO CCDCOE in Tallinn.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Zero successful critical infrastructure breaches since 2007 attack. 2022 cyberattacks during KGB/Russia escalation: CERT-EE mitigated DDoS in under 1 hour. ISKE compliance: 95% of government systems. Data Embassy concept: Estonian data stored abroad preserves government continuity if territory compromised. Estonia ranks global top-3 in cybersecurity readiness (ITU GCI 2024).
global_cases.failure_modes: ISKE compliance bureaucratic burden: smaller municipalities find 300+ requirements difficult to implement without dedicated IT staff. International knowledge transfer is limited — NATO CCDCOE tools not shareable with non-NATO countries. Private sector lagged government by 5+ years in cybersecurity baseline.
global_cases.replicability_factors: CERT-EE model is globally documented (ENISA reference). ISKE security baseline framework adapted by Georgia, Latvia, Lithuania. Non-NATO countries can access CERT-EE knowledge via EU-bilateral channels. Data Embassy concept (government data in friendly third-country data centres) is directly applicable to UZ/KG sovereignty concerns.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ cybersecurity law (2022) and UNICON.UZ (national cybersecurity SOC) provide the institutional foundation. CERT-EE architecture is the direct reference for UZ CERT enhancement. Data Embassy concept — backing up EPIGU and critical registries in a neutral foreign data centre — is politically appealing as sovereignty protection. EU bilateral cybersecurity cooperation programme (DigiConnect4CA) provides donor pathway. Budget: $5-10M for UZ CERT enhancement with Estonian advisory.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG's Цифровой Кодекс (2025) includes cybersecurity requirements. KG needs a functional CERT (currently exists on paper, limited capacity). Estonian CERT model — small team, automation-first, international threat intel sharing — is directly applicable at KG scale. Budget: $3-5M. Donor pathway: EU DigiConnect4CA, NATO Partners across the Globe programme (KG is a NATO partner country).
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian-language security monitoring tools. Non-NATO threat intelligence sharing protocols (ENISA bilateral is option). ISKE-equivalent security baseline for KG/UZ government systems. Sovereign data location requirements (can't use NATO CCDCOE Cyber Range directly — needs bilateral or private alternative).

NATO CCDCOE Tallinn — Official

global_cases.case_name: Ukraine Diia Digital ID Under Wartime Conditions (Resilience Case)
global_cases.problem_solved: Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 created an unprecedented test for digital government: 6M+ IDPs (internally displaced persons) needed to prove identity, access benefits, and register with authorities while physical document offices were destroyed or inaccessible. Diia's digital ID proved to be a critical tool for continuity of civil registration and social payments.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Diia emergency adaptation: (1) Digital Identity — Diia digital passport legally equivalent to physical, accepted at border crossings and police checkpoints; (2) IDP Registration — digital registration of displaced persons at any mobile device with location data; (3) Emergency Payments — direct digital payments (5,000 UAH/person) to Diia-verified citizens bypassing destroyed banking infrastructure; (4) Damage Documentation — citizens photograph destroyed property via Diia for insurance/reparations processing; (5) Wartime Certificate — digital military service exemptions and veteran status. All served via AWS GovCloud with European backups. 14M Diia users actively using wartime features.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 6M+ IDPs registered digitally. $550M+ in emergency payments disbursed via Diia. 1.2M damage reports submitted. Digital ID accepted at Polish, German, Czech borders. Zero major security breaches of Diia during the period. MinTsifry received NATO award for digital resilience 2023.
global_cases.failure_modes: Elderly/low-literacy IDPs needed physical support at digital assistance centres. Internet access blackouts in frontline regions prevented some Diia use. Hostile DDOS attacks targeting Diia multiple times (all mitigated). Diia could not serve 40%+ of evacuees without smartphone access.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Ukraine MinTsifry has published full technical post-mortem. Digital ID for emergency management is applicable to any country facing natural disaster, conflict, or mass displacement. Directly applicable to KG earthquake/flood disaster scenarios and UZ emergency management.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ faces natural disaster risk (earthquakes in Tashkent, Ferghana Valley; flooding in Aral Sea basin). EPIGU + MyID emergency services module — enabling digital identity verification, benefit payments, and property damage documentation during disasters — is directly applicable. Budget: $2-3M to add disaster-response module to existing EPIGU. World Bank Disaster Risk Management project provides donor pathway.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG faces significant disaster risk: earthquakes (near Bishkek fault zone), GLOF events, and mudslides. Diia wartime architecture maps to KG peacetime disaster scenarios. The key lesson: IDP/disaster victim digital registration should work OFFLINE for when connectivity is disrupted. Budget: $1.5-2.5M disaster-resilience module for KG Tunduk services. World Bank disaster risk project is the donor pathway.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Offline-first design (critical difference from Diia's online-dependent architecture). Russian/Kyrgyz language. Integration with MChS (Ministry of Emergencies) database. Satellite connectivity backup (Starlink-equivalent) for disaster zone coverage.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Biometric Border Control (SafePass & AutoPass)
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan international airports and major border crossings faced long queues (1-3 hours) for passport control. Border officers performed manual document inspection without biometric verification, relying on visual passport matching. Biometric AutoPass systems deployed AI facial recognition to verify identity and screen against watchlists in 10-15 seconds per person.
global_cases.architecture_summary: AutoPass kiosks at international airports (Nur-Sultan, Almaty): self-service passport scan + live facial recognition vs passport chip photo. Watchlist screening against INTERPOL SLTD (Stolen and Lost Travel Documents) + KZ national security watchlist. Integration with CAMS (Consolidated Automated Migration System) for real-time traveller risk scoring. Border Crossing System: police data exchange with EAEU common crossing database. Mobile version: Pre-registration QR code for frequent travellers (e-Mektebi frequent traveller programme). Vendor: NEC (Japan) facial recognition engine.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Average border crossing time: reduced from 3 minutes to 40 seconds for pre-registered travellers. Queue wait time at Nur-Sultan Airport: 45 minutes to 12 minutes peak. Watchlist alerts: 1,200+ positive matches in 2 years. INTERPOL SLTD hits: 340 stolen documents detected. Traveller pre-registration: 2M+ profiles. System uptime: 99.4%.
global_cases.failure_modes: Facial recognition accuracy for darker skin tones: 8% higher false rejection rate (NEC engine bias, documented by NIST). Integration with EAEU database required 18 months of bilateral negotiations. Kiosks malfunction in extreme cold (Nur-Sultan winters -30°C) — 15% hardware failure rate in first winter. Data sharing with Russian FSB under EAEU protocols raised privacy concerns.
global_cases.replicability_factors: NEC has global deployments. KZ architecture using standard ICAO biometric passport data is directly applicable to any ICAO-compliant border crossing. Directly applicable to UZ and KG airport modernisation.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Tashkent International Airport handles 5M+ passengers/year. UZ MIA has mandate for border modernisation. Biometric AutoPass is procurable under WB or EU transport project funding. NEC, Thales, and IDEMIA all have Central Asia presence. Budget: $10-15M for Tashkent + Samarkand airport biometric border. Avoid facial recognition at land borders (privacy risk, accuracy concerns) — airports only for Phase 1.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Manas International Airport (Bishkek) handles 2M+ passengers/year. KG border with China (Irkeshtam, Torugart) processes significant cargo and passenger flow. Biometric border at Manas Airport is achievable for $5-8M. Land border with China and Kazakhstan is high-priority for cargo risk scoring (not facial recognition — RFID-based commercial vehicle pre-clearance is better model here).
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: ICAO biometric passport compliance (both UZ and KG already issue biometric passports). Avoid skin-tone-biased facial recognition (insist on NIST-tested engine with <1% false rejection differential). EAEU and SCO watchlist integration protocols. Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language operator interfaces.

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Aral Sea Restoration AI Monitoring
global_cases.problem_solved: The Aral Sea (shared by KZ and UZ) shrank to 10% of its original size due to Soviet-era irrigation diversion. The North Aral Sea (KZ side) partially recovered after the Kokaral Dam (2005) but required continuous environmental monitoring: water level, salinity, biodiversity, and dust storm frequency. Manual monitoring was infrequent and expensive. AI satellite analysis enabled continuous environmental change detection.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Satellite change detection platform: Sentinel-1 (SAR) + Sentinel-2 (optical) + Landsat time series for water surface monitoring. Change detection algorithm: NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) time series analysis with anomaly detection. Air quality monitoring: MODIS aerosol optical depth for dust storm detection from dried seabed. Biodiversity: drone survey AI for vegetation and bird population counting. Data portal: public-access dashboard showing water level trend, salinity estimates, dust storm frequency. World Bank co-funded component for UZ Southern Aral.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Continuous water level monitoring: North Aral at 1-week update frequency. Dust storm prediction accuracy: 78% for 48-hour advance warning. Biodiversity survey: 45 bird species confirmed returning to North Aral. Annual environmental reporting: cost reduced 70% vs field surveys. Data shared with IFAS (International Fund for Aral Sea Saving — all 5 CA countries).
global_cases.failure_modes: SAR satellite analysis requires specialist geophysicist interpretation — technical skills shortage in regional environment agencies. Cross-border data sharing with UZ: restricted on some datasets for sovereignty reasons. Dust storm predictions insufficient for agriculture planning (need 5-day advance warning).
global_cases.replicability_factors: All satellite data is free (Copernicus). Algorithm published in ISPRS and RSE journals. IFAS coordination mechanism exists for CA-wide rollout. World Bank Environment project funding available.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ is the most directly affected country by Aral Sea disaster (Southern Aral dried completely). Satellite monitoring of Southern Aral dust storms is a PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY (Karakalpakstan respiratory disease rates are 3x national average from dust exposure). World Bank NSDI project includes environment monitoring component. IFAS provides multilateral framework. Budget: included in existing World Bank projects — incremental cost is $1-2M for AI analytics layer.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG's environmental monitoring priorities are different (mountain glacier retreat, lake level changes, forest degradation) but the satellite monitoring architecture is identical. Issyk-Kul lake monitoring, Tien Shan glacier retreat tracking, and Toktogul reservoir level monitoring are all achievable with the same AI satellite analysis pipeline. Budget: $2-4M for KG environmental AI monitoring. UNDP, GEF, ADB environment projects.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language environmental monitoring dashboard. Integration with national hydrometeorological service data. Extension of dust storm prediction to 5-day window (requires better NWP model). Public access dashboard for civil society and media (transparency requirement).

World Bank — Aral Sea Basin

global_cases.case_name: Rotterdam Climate Adaptation Digital Twin
global_cases.problem_solved: Rotterdam (90% below sea level) needed to plan and monitor climate adaptation infrastructure (green roofs, water squares, permeable pavements, underground storage) across the city. Different departments maintained separate data on infrastructure, land use, and climate risk with no integrated view for planning or emergency response.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Rotterdam Climate Digital Twin: FIWARE (open-source IoT platform) aggregating sensor data from 200+ rain gauges, 500+ water level sensors, 1,200+ environmental sensors. 3D city model (CityGML format) with overlay of flood risk zones, green infrastructure coverage, and heat island intensity. AI modules: flash flood prediction (4-hour advance warning, ML on sensor + NWP data), urban heat island mapping (ML on temperature sensors + satellite), green infrastructure performance measurement. Open data portal: all sensor data publicly accessible. Policy application: developers must show digital twin impact assessment for new buildings.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Flash flood early warning: activated 12 times, 0 false alarms in pilot period. Urban heat reduction measurement: green infrastructure verified 2.3°C reduction in pilot district. Building permit assessment: 500+ new buildings screened via digital twin. Climate investment prioritisation: $180M in city infrastructure spending optimised via digital twin modelling.
global_cases.failure_modes: FIWARE platform complexity: open-source flexibility comes with integration complexity — required 18-month technical build. High sensor density cost ($28M hardware + platform). 3D city model requires continuous update — 5-year data staleness creates planning errors. Private landowner green infrastructure not captured (only public land monitored).
global_cases.replicability_factors: FIWARE is free open-source. Rotterdam Climate Centre publishes case studies. Applicable to Tashkent and Bishkek where flash flooding and heat island are documented urban risks.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Tashkent summer temperatures (45°C peak in 2024) create urban heat crisis. Flash floods in Ferghana Valley are a seasonal hazard. Rotterdam's sensor network + flash flood warning is directly applicable. Start with flash flood early warning (highest urgency) then add heat island mapping. Budget: $5-8M for Tashkent urban climate monitoring pilot. Donor pathway: ADB urban, World Bank DRM, GEF.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Bishkek faces both flash flooding (debris flows from Ala-Too mountains) and heat island effects. Rotterdam's architecture is applicable at Bishkek city scale for $4-6M. The mountain-city flash flood model (different dynamics from Rotterdam sea-level flooding) requires adaptation. UNDP urban resilience programmes are donor pathways.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Adaptation for mountain flash flood dynamics (different from Rotterdam coastal flooding). Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language public dashboard. Open data policy for sensor data. Urban planning regulation requiring digital twin assessment for new construction.

sources.title: Rotterdam Climate Adaptation Strategy
Deltares Urban Climate Adaptation

global_cases.case_name: India ISRO Bhuvan Geoportal & Environment Monitoring
global_cases.problem_solved: India needed a national geospatial platform for environment monitoring, forest cover change detection, land degradation assessment, and disaster management that used India's sovereign satellite data (Resourcesat, Cartosat) rather than relying on international commercial providers. Bhuvan provided a Google Earth equivalent operated by ISRO with Indian satellite imagery.
global_cases.architecture_summary: National web GIS platform: Bhuvan portal (bhuvan.nrsc.gov.in) with Indian satellite imagery archive (15+ years), vector datasets, and analysis tools. Environment modules: forest cover change detection (bi-annual), land degradation assessment, wetland mapping, coastal change monitoring, Aral Sea equivalent (Chilika Lake seasonal mapping). AI layer: automated change detection between time-series imagery, forest encroachment alert system, crop yield estimation from satellite. API: open access for government agencies, researchers. Disaster Management Support (DMS): real-time flood and cyclone mapping during events.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 15TB+ of satellite imagery accessible to government users. Forest change detection: 98% of India's forests mapped bi-annually. 10,000+ government users. Disaster response: cyclone Fani (2019) — flood mapping updated every 6 hours. Forest encroachment alerts: 5,000+ alerts issued to forest departments. India's land degradation atlas produced using Bhuvan data cited in IPCC reports.
global_cases.failure_modes: Commercial satellite imagery quality: ISRO satellites have lower resolution (5.8m) than commercial providers (0.3m) for some applications. User interface dated — adoption low among non-specialist users. Cross-ministry data silos: Forest, Agriculture, Disaster ministries maintain separate Bhuvan instances with no unified view. Cloud processing added late — initial architecture was batch downloads only.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Bhuvan open architecture published by ISRO. Developing countries can access Indian satellite data under bilateral agreements. ESA Copernicus provides equivalent free satellite data globally. This architecture is the reference for building a sovereign geo-analytics platform without commercial satellite dependency.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ World Bank NSDI project ($35M, 2025-2030) is building exactly this — a national spatial data infrastructure. Bhuvan architecture + ESA Copernicus data (free) is the technical foundation. The AI change detection modules for cotton field monitoring, Aral Sea monitoring, and land degradation are directly applicable. Budget is covered by WB project — additional AI analytics layer is $2-3M incremental cost.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG needs environment monitoring for glacier retreat, deforestation in Fergana range, and pasture degradation. Bhuvan architecture using free Copernicus data is feasible for KG at $3-5M. GEF and World Bank environment projects are funding sources. Key application: pasture degradation monitoring for KG's 9M cattle/sheep.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Use ESA Copernicus data (globally free) rather than Indian ISRO satellites. Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language geoportal. Adaptation of change detection algorithms for CA landscapes (Central Asian steppe vs Indian tropical/semi-arid). Integration with national hydrometeorological services data.

ISRO Application Programmes

global_cases.case_name: China BeiDou Navigation + Environmental Monitoring in Central Asia
global_cases.problem_solved: China promoted BeiDou satellite navigation as a GPS alternative across BRI partner countries. In Central Asia, BeiDou-based applications were deployed for agricultural monitoring, flood early warning in mountain areas, and infrastructure monitoring along the Karakoram Highway and China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan rail corridors.
global_cases.architecture_summary: BeiDou III constellation (2020 fully operational): precision navigation + SMS capability + short-message emergency service for remote areas without cellular coverage. CA applications: (1) Agricultural IoT: BeiDou-connected soil sensors for precision farming along BRI agricultural zones; (2) Slope stability monitoring: BeiDou GNSS displacement sensors on mountain slopes along CKU (China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan) planned rail route; (3) Fleet management: BeiDou tracking for cross-border transport. No cellular coverage required — BeiDou provides direct satellite communication link.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: BeiDou used in UZ precision agriculture pilots: 15,000 ha with BeiDou-connected sensors. Slope monitoring: 200 critical slope sites monitored along planned CKU rail corridor. Emergency SMS: field workers in Tien Shan mountains (no cellular) using BeiDou for distress messaging. CA coverage: all of UZ and KG covered with BeiDou signal.
global_cases.failure_modes: Geopolitical sensitivity: Western donors discourage BeiDou adoption in CA projects they fund (sanctions risk for US-listed components). Data sovereignty: BeiDou applications route some telemetry data via Chinese ground stations. Device supply chain: BeiDou-enabled devices sourced from Chinese manufacturers only.
global_cases.replicability_factors: BeiDou provides free civilian positioning service globally. For remote CA areas without GPS/cellular coverage, BeiDou emergency messaging is the ONLY option. The agricultural monitoring architecture is vendor-neutral if BeiDou is used as positioning layer only.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: BeiDou is ALREADY in use in UZ. The monitoring applications (agriculture IoT, slope stability) are relevant. However, Western donor projects will not procure BeiDou-primary systems. Score 6: medium transferability with geopolitical caveat. UZ can use BeiDou for applications funded without Western donor restrictions (national budget, IsDB, AIIB, EDB).
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Same caveat. KG remote mountain areas where GPS accuracy is poor and cellular is absent — BeiDou emergency messaging is the only option. Slope monitoring along CKU rail corridor is a Chinese-funded project that naturally uses BeiDou. Score 6 with same geopolitical asterisk.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Data sovereignty protocol — ensure BeiDou telemetry does not route through Chinese state servers. Use BeiDou positioning layer with sovereign data storage. Avoid BeiDou for applications where Western donor restrictions apply.

global_cases.case_name: Finland Aurora AI — National AI Strategy for Public Services
global_cases.problem_solved: Finland needed to apply AI systematically across government services, particularly in areas where Finland has competitive advantage: forestry management, cold-climate agriculture, and environmental data analytics. The Aurora AI programme identified 150+ government AI use cases and piloted the highest-priority ones across 10 government agencies.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Government AI coordination programme: Aurora AI task force under Prime Minister's Office identifying AI opportunities across all ministries. Key environmental implementations: (1) MAVI satellite-based agricultural subsidy verification (replacing field inspections); (2) Forestry AI: drone + satellite analysis of forest health, illegal logging detection; (3) Helsinki environmental twin (building permit environmental impact AI). Technical platform: Azure Government for most AI deployments. Open AI register: Finland publishes list of all government AI systems (algorithmic transparency). AI ethics board reviews all citizen-facing AI.
vendors_involved: Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 150 AI use cases assessed; 20 in production by 2021. MAVI agricultural subsidy AI: 400,000 field inspections replaced by satellite verification, saving €35M/year. Forestry drone monitoring: 3M hectares monitored annually at 20% of manual cost. Government AI register: 40+ systems published publicly. Finland ranks global top-5 for government AI readiness.
global_cases.failure_modes: Voluntary AI ethics review: 30% of agencies skipped review. Azure Government dependency creates commercial lock-in. Some AI systems implemented without adequate training data (low-data rural areas). Public sector workers resisted AI workload tools fearing job displacement.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Finland publishes AI register publicly — methodology replicable. MAVI satellite subsidy verification architecture directly applicable to UZ cotton subsidy fraud detection. Nordic Council of Ministers has co-funded AI programme replication in Baltic and Arctic states.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Finland's MAVI agricultural subsidy satellite verification is the MOST DIRECTLY APPLICABLE component for UZ: $35M/year savings from eliminating field inspections maps proportionally to $100M+/year potential for UZ cotton subsidies. The forestry AI is applicable to UZ's Uzbekistan afforestation programme (Yashil Makon). Budget: $3-5M for UZ satellite subsidy verification (agriculture component). Finland's open AI register concept is a governance good practice UZ could adopt for trust-building.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Finland's forestry drone monitoring is applicable to KG's deforestation crisis in Fergana range and Chui Valley. The open AI register transparency model is directly applicable — KG Цифровой Кодекс (2025) includes provisions for AI accountability. Budget: $2-4M for KG environmental AI monitoring. Nordic-Baltic cooperation channel provides diplomatic pathway.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language AI system interfaces. Open AI register adapted to CIS legal context. Avoid Azure dependency — sovereign cloud compliance required for UZ/KG government systems. Adaptation of forestry models for Central Asian vegetation types (juniper forest vs Finnish boreal).

global_cases.case_name: Kyrgyzstan GLOF (Glacial Lake Outburst Flood) Early Warning System
global_cases.problem_solved: Kyrgyzstan has 2,000+ glacial lakes fed by 8,000+ glaciers in the Tien Shan. Glacial retreat (accelerating at 0.8%/year) is increasing GLOF events — sudden, catastrophic floods from glacial lake outbursts that destroy downstream villages with minutes of warning. The KG Hydromet Service needed automated lake monitoring and early warning to give downstream communities 30+ minutes notice.
global_cases.architecture_summary: UNDP/GEF funded pilot: satellite lake area monitoring (Sentinel-2 time series, lake area growth anomaly detection), 30 high-priority lakes instrumented with GPS-tracked shore sensors + acoustic water level gauges. AI module: lake area + inflow rate change detection triggering alert, downstream flood routing model (using DEM + HydroSHEDS drainage basin data). Alert propagation: SMS alerts to ayil aymak (local government) and village Telegram groups. Integration with KG Hydromet national early warning system.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 30 high-risk lakes monitored continuously. GLOF event detected and warned: 3 events 2021-2023, all with 45+ minutes advance warning (vs 0 previously). No casualties in monitored areas during those events (vs 12 deaths in unmonitored comparable events in same period). Phase 2: expanding to 100 lakes planned.
global_cases.failure_modes: Sensor power in remote areas: solar panels at 4,000m elevation have limited winter generation. Satellite cloud cover during storm events (exactly when GLOFs occur) reduces detection reliability. Alert propagation to non-smartphone communities requires multiple channels. False alarm rate: 3 false alarms in 3 years creating community fatigue.
global_cases.replicability_factors: This IS a KG case — demonstrates donor-funded environmental AI at small scale. Architecture is replicable for any mountain country with glacial lake hazard. Directly relevant to UZ (Fergana Valley receives water from KG mountains) as shared risk.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ Ferghana Valley receives floodwaters from KG mountain GLOF events — UZ is a downstream stakeholder in KG's GLOF warning system. Bilateral data sharing: KG GLOF alerts should automatically trigger UZ downstream alert for Ferghana communities. Budget: $1-2M for UZ downstream alert integration with KG GLOF system. World Bank DRM project funding.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: This IS a KG case — Phase 2 expansion to 100 lakes is the ACTIVE PROCUREMENT. The Phase 2 sensor network, satellite monitoring platform, and community alert system expansion is a $15-20M procurement. GEF, UNDP, World Bank DRM project are potential funders. This is one of the most urgent and directly actionable cases in the KG portfolio.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Phase 2 adaptation: satellite cloud-penetrating SAR (Sentinel-1) as primary detection during storm events. Community alert via Telegram + radio (not just SMS). Power reliability: fuel cell backup for remote sensors. Kyrgyz language alerts.

global_cases.case_name: New Zealand MfE AI Emissions Reporting
global_cases.problem_solved: New Zealand's Ministry for the Environment (MfE) needed to improve greenhouse gas inventory accuracy, especially for agricultural emissions (methane from livestock — 50% of NZ's GHG). AI-assisted satellite and sensor data analysis could improve agricultural emission estimates beyond traditional activity-based calculations.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Multi-source emissions monitoring: agricultural CH4 estimates using satellite methane column measurements (TROPOMI Sentinel-5P), livestock density maps (from aerial survey + ML), land use change detection. Urban emissions: traffic emissions AI using vehicle counts × emission factors × congestion multipliers. Industrial: automated reconciliation between industry-reported data and satellite NO2/SO2 measurements for anomaly flagging. All integrated into NZ Greenhouse Gas Inventory system. Public dashboard: real-time emissions tracking by sector/region.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Agricultural emissions estimate uncertainty: reduced from ±15% to ±8%. Anomaly detection: 3 industrial facilities flagged for under-reporting (regulatory action taken). NZ GHG Inventory quality: upgraded from Tier 1 to Tier 2/3 for 60% of emission categories. Public dashboard: 50,000+ monthly users tracking regional emissions.
global_cases.failure_modes: TROPOMI satellite resolution (7km) insufficient for point-source attribution in dense agricultural areas. Cloud cover over NZ's hilly terrain reduces satellite measurement frequency. Industry-reported data quality highly variable — some sectors self-report inaccurately without penalty.
global_cases.replicability_factors: TROPOMI satellite data is free (Copernicus). Architecture applicable to any country needing Paris Agreement-compliant GHG monitoring. Central Asian agricultural methane (cotton and livestock) is a specific application.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has livestock and cotton agriculture emissions that are poorly quantified. Paris Agreement reporting requires improved GHG inventory. NZ architecture using free TROPOMI data is applicable for $3-5M. Donor pathway: GEF, ADB climate finance. Key: UZ GHG reporting accuracy is needed for accessing climate finance (carbon credit markets, green bonds).
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has significant livestock methane emissions (9M livestock) and hydro power sector (which has its own reservoir methane emissions). Paris Agreement reporting improvement. Donor pathway: GEF, World Bank. Budget: $2-3M.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz interface. Adaptation for cotton agriculture emission factors (not in NZ model). Integration with national statistical system for activity data. Climate finance (carbon credit) market connection to monetise emission reductions.

global_cases.case_name: Uzbekistan eTravelUzbekistan Digital Tourism Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Uzbekistan's tourism sector was severely underdeveloped relative to the Silk Road heritage (Samarkand, Bukhara, Khiva — UNESCO World Heritage Sites). Visa processes were opaque, ticketing for heritage sites was paper-only, and tourist data was uncollected. The State Committee for Tourism and Tourism Development needed digital infrastructure to grow tourism from 1.7M (2016) to 7.5M visitors (2025 target).
global_cases.architecture_summary: e-Visa system (e.visa.gov.uz) — online application replacing embassy visits for 90+ countries; digital heritage site ticketing (e-ticket for all major sites with QR code entry); eTravelUzbekistan.com — integrated booking platform for hotels, guides, and tours with UZ Tax Committee e-receipt integration; AI recommendation engine for itinerary planning. Automated tourist statistics collection from e-ticket data. Mobile app: UzRoad navigator integrated with cultural site AR overlays. Integration with MyID for foreign visitor identity verification.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: e-Visa: 2M+ applications processed. Tourist arrivals: 1.7M (2016) → 5.3M (2023), trending toward 7M target. Heritage site revenue: +340% from ticketing digitisation (eliminated scalpers and entry fraud). Hotel digital registration: 80% of tourist accommodation compliant. Foreign tourist spending tracked via bank data: $2.1B in 2023.
global_cases.failure_modes: AR overlays at heritage sites were technically poor in launch version — abandoned after negative tourist reviews. Hotel digital registration compliance enforcement slow in small towns. Mobile connectivity at some remote heritage sites (Khiva) insufficient for digital ticket scanning — offline mode required.
global_cases.replicability_factors: This IS a UZ case — provided as self-assessment. Key lesson: e-Visa is the highest-ROI single technology investment for any tourism-dependent government — reduces friction from every potential visitor.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: This IS the UZ case. Key next phase: AI-powered tourist itinerary assistant (multilingual — Russian, English, Chinese, Arabic) leveraging heritage site ticketing data for personalised recommendations. AI chatbot for tourist inquiries accessible via Telegram. Budget: $3-5M for AI tourism assistant on top of existing digital infrastructure.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has significant tourism potential (Issyk-Kul, Tien Shan ecotourism, nomadic culture). UZ e-Visa architecture is directly replicable. KG needs: online visa + digital heritage ticketing + booking aggregator. Budget: $3-5M. Donor pathway: ADB tourism development project, World Bank.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: KG: Kyrgyz language AI interface for local tourism operators. Nomadic culture AR — unique KG heritage product. Offline mode mandatory (Tien Shan mountain sites have no connectivity). Integration with KG border control for foreign visitor tracking.

global_cases.case_name: Saudi Arabia Absher Tourism App & Digital Heritage
global_cases.problem_solved: Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030 needed to open tourism to international visitors (previously restricted), issue tourist visas digitally, and digitise heritage site access (AlUla, Diriyah, Hegra) to attract 100M visitors/year by 2030. Cultural heritage was poorly digitised and visitor data uncollected.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Absher multi-purpose super-app (originally an ID/government services app) extended to tourism: e-Visa for 49 countries online, digital entry tickets for heritage sites with QR verification, AI multilingual tourist information chatbot (Arabic/English/Chinese/French), IoT-managed visitor flow control at heritage sites (density sensors triggering timed entry). AlUla app: AR overlays on Nabataean rock sculptures with AI object recognition to identify carvings. Heritage management AI: drone surveillance of restricted archaeological zones detecting unauthorized access.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Saudi tourist arrivals: 14.8M (2019) → 25M (2023) → target 150M (2030). e-Visa processing: 12 million issued 2019-2023. AlUla AR app: 500,000 downloads. Heritage site revenue: 5x increase post-digitisation. Absher: 20M registered users. Visitor flow control: UNESCO commended AI density management at sensitive sites.
global_cases.failure_modes: e-Visa system overwhelmed during initial launch (website crashes for first 3 days). Cultural heritage AI chatbot: accuracy dropped significantly for non-English queries about local customs. Heritage drone surveillance: false alarms triggered by wildlife — required operator tuning. IBM Watson chatbot required extensive Arabic cultural customisation.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Saudi e-Visa architecture (MENA context) is replicable. Absher super-app heritage extension is a documented case. UNESCO World Heritage site AI visitor management is directly applicable to UZ and KG UNESCO sites.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Samarkand, Bukhara, Shakhrisabz, Itchan Kala, Shah-i-Zinda). Saudi AI visitor flow management is directly applicable to managing tourism at sensitive archaeological sites. UZ AI chatbot for tourism (Russian/Uzbek/English/Chinese/Arabic) is the key product opportunity. Budget: $5-8M for AI heritage tourism platform. Tourism Committee has budget and political priority.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has no UNESCO World Heritage Sites but has strong ecotourism potential. Saudi model is over-engineered for KG's tourism scale. Key applicable element: AI multilingual tourism chatbot (Russian/Kyrgyz/English) and digital ticketing for Issyk-Kul resort zone management. Budget: $2-3M. ADB tourism project as pathway.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz/Chinese/Arabic multilingual chatbot training on local cultural knowledge. Visitor density management for fragile archaeological sites. Offline mode for mountain and remote heritage locations. Integration with national ID system for visitor data collection.

global_cases.case_name: Greece Gov.gr Rapid Digital Transformation (COVID Era)
global_cases.problem_solved: Greece's tourism sector was threatened by COVID-19 — 30% of GDP dependent on tourism. The government needed to rapidly digitise government services AND create a tourism certification infrastructure (vaccination certificate + test result + COVID-free border crossing) to allow tourists to arrive safely. Gov.gr became the platform for both citizen services and COVID tourism management in 18 months.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Gov.gr platform (accelerated COVID build): citizen authentication via TaxisNet + Gsis identity provider, digital COVID certificate (QR-verified, aligned with EU COVID passport standard), tourism reopening portal, vaccination status API for airlines and hotels. AI element: tourist inflow modelling to predict island healthcare capacity demand. Key speed achievement: built in 120 days by 250-person team, launched May 2020 before summer tourism season. Post-COVID: evolved into national citizen services portal with 500+ services. Architecture: microservices on AWS Greece region.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Gov.gr: 13M registered users (Greece pop 11M). 500+ government services. COVID certificate: 15M certificates issued. Tourism 2021: 18.2M visitors (90% of 2019 despite COVID). Gov.gr won EU Horizon Award for public sector innovation 2022. Digital service delivery cost: reduced 65%. Citizen satisfaction: 89%.
global_cases.failure_modes: 120-day build led to technical debt requiring €45M refactoring investment in 2022-2023. AWS dependency: Greece created sovereign data obligations but Cloud Act uncertainty for US-hosted data. Post-COVID momentum partially lost when emergency urgency removed — some agencies reverted to paper processes.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Greece's 120-day emergency build demonstrates what's achievable with political will and a small competent team. The COVID certification architecture is directly replicable for any health certification system. EU member state model provides less transferable governance elements.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: Greece's tourism COVID certification is less relevant now but the SPEED OF BUILD lesson (120-day MVP with 250-person team) is directly applicable to UZ EPIGU expansion. UZ government has stated intent to rapidly expand digital services — Greece demonstrates the execution model. The specific tourism module (AI inflow modelling for heritage site capacity) is applicable to UZ Samarkand tourism management.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: Speed-of-build lesson applicable. KG tourism COVID certification (post-COVID health certificate for visitors) architecture is the reference. AI tourist inflow modelling for Issyk-Kul resort zone capacity management is the specific application.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Avoid AWS for sovereign data. Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language for citizens. Emergency-build approach: identify 5-10 highest-priority services and build fast rather than planning all 500 services upfront. Technical debt management plan from Day 1.

EU Joinup — Greece Gov.gr Case Study

global_cases.case_name: Kyrgyzstan Nomadic Heritage Digital Archive & Tourism AI
global_cases.problem_solved: Kyrgyzstan's intangible cultural heritage — Manas epic, komuz music, eagle hunting, nomadic yurt traditions — was underdocumented and inaccessible to international tourists and researchers. Digital archiving and AI-assisted multilingual presentation of nomadic culture could differentiate KG tourism from mass-market alternatives and support UNESCO nomination processes.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Emerging government-NGO programme: National Library KG + UNDP digital archive project — 3D scanning of artifacts, audio/video archive of Manas oral recitations, AI-generated multilingual audio guides (Russian, English, Chinese, Korean). AR application for displaying 3D yurt construction and eagle hunting techniques at World Nomad Games venues. AI content: NLP-based query-answering system trained on Kyrgyz oral literature corpus. Platform: local hosting at KG GIIN (State Institute of Intellectual Property). UNDP and UNESCO co-funded.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: EARLY STAGE: 50,000 digitised cultural artifacts. Manas audio archive: 200 hours recorded from 15 manaschi (oral performers). AR app: developed but limited distribution. World Nomad Games digital attendance: 300,000+ online viewers. KG UNESCO application for Manas: supported by digital documentation.
global_cases.failure_modes: Sustainability: UNDP funding ended 2023 — no government budget for maintenance. Kyrgyz-language NLP models immature — AI query-answering quality poor. AR app too technically complex for tourist hardware (requires high-end smartphone). Content digitisation ongoing but at slow pace.
global_cases.replicability_factors: This IS a KG case. Key lesson: intangible cultural heritage needs SIMPLE digital presentation (web + audio + basic video), not complex AR, to be sustainable. The nomadic heritage AI chatbot concept is a viable tourism product if built on robust Kyrgyz NLP foundation.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has rich tangible heritage (architecture) vs KG's intangible heritage (oral tradition). UZ can learn from KG's experience: don't over-invest in AR before content is properly digitised. UZ's priority is digital guide/chatbot for Samarkand and Bukhara using existing digitised content.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: This IS the KG case and represents an active gap/opportunity. Phase 2 of the nomadic heritage digital programme — building on UNDP's 50,000 artifacts with AI-generated multilingual tour guidance — is the procurement opportunity. Budget: $3-5M. UNESCO and UNDP would co-fund. Tourism revenue potential from differentiated 'nomadic AI guide' product is $20-30M/year in tourist spending.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Build Kyrgyz-language NLP FIRST before AI guide products (depends on Bhashini-equivalent for Kyrgyz). Simple web+audio distribution before AR. Government maintenance budget as condition of any further donor investment. Partnership with KG tourism operators for commercial integration.

UNESCO ICH Kyrgyzstan

global_cases.case_name: UAE Louvre Abu Dhabi AI Visitor Experience
global_cases.problem_solved: Louvre Abu Dhabi (opened 2017) needed to create a world-class multilingual visitor experience for a culturally diverse visitor base (Arabic, French, English, Russian, Chinese, South Asian languages) while positioning Abu Dhabi as a global cultural destination. AI-powered multilingual guide and personalized artwork recommendation system replaced traditional audio guide rentals.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Mobile app with AI guide: NLP-based artwork query system (visitor photographs artwork → AI identifies + provides multilingual description + related works). Personalized tour recommendation: ML model based on visitor's time available, interests stated at entry, previous artwork interactions. Crowd management: beacon-based visitor tracking (anonymous) feeds density model for staff deployment. Partnership with Artlens AI (Cleveland Museum model). Multilingual NLP: 9 languages including Arabic (MSA + dialects). Backend: Azure + AWS hybrid.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: App download rate: 65% of visitors. Satisfaction rating with AI guide: 4.3/5. Average visitor time in museum: 2.7 hours (up from 1.9 hours). Multilingual query resolution: 88% of questions answered without staff intervention. Revenue from guided app premium tier: $1.2M/year. Visitor return rate: 35% increased from 22%.
global_cases.failure_modes: AI artwork identification accuracy dropped for non-Western artifacts from the African and Asian collections (training data bias toward Western art history). Arabic dialect NLP was lower quality than standard Arabic. Battery drain on visitors' phones using AR features. Image recognition confused similar-style artifacts.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Artlens AI platform is commercially available. Multilingual AI guide is replicable for any heritage institution. Russian-language component makes it directly applicable to UZ heritage sites with Russian-speaking tourism base.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ Samarkand/Bukhara heritage institutions could deploy equivalent: visitor photographs Islamic tilework → AI explains Timurid architectural motifs in Russian/Uzbek/English/Chinese/Arabic. App download penetration at major sites (Registan, Kalon Minaret) could easily reach 50%+. Budget: $2-4M for AI heritage guide (Artlens-equivalent or custom). Tourism Committee has budget authority.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG heritage institutions are smaller and less digitised than UZ. Simpler audio guide with AI multilingual translation is achievable first ($500k-1M) before investing in full AR heritage guide. World Nomad Games venue guide app would be the pilot application.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Central Asian Islamic architecture training data for AI (currently dominated by Western art databases). Offline mode for sites without reliable connectivity. Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz/Chinese/Arabic multilingual NLP. Integration with national tourism platform for booking upsell.

Artlens AI — Cleveland Museum of Art

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Enbek Labour Market Digital Platform
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan needed a unified labour market information system that would provide real-time employment analytics, skills gap identification, and AI-assisted job matching. Existing employment centres were paper-based with significant backlogs, and unemployment benefits were distributed without fraud detection or reemployment monitoring.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Enbek.kz platform (Ministry of Labour and Social Protection): job portal (employer posts + jobseeker profiles), ML job-skills matching algorithm (collaborative filtering on 500k+ job-seeker profiles), digital social contract for unemployed (digital sign-up for training vouchers + unemployment benefit + job placement commitment). Integration with GNK (tax committee) for payroll verification and benefit fraud detection. AI component: skills gap analytics by region and sector, predicting labour demand 12 months ahead. Mobile app for employers: instant hire with digital employment contract generation.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 3.5M registered jobseekers. 200,000+ employers. Annual job placements via Enbek: 800,000+. Unemployment benefit fraud detection: 35,000 fraudulent claims identified (saving KZT 18B). Skills gap reports: used by 15 universities to revise curricula. Employment rate of benefit recipients: 62% reemployed within 6 months (vs 48% pre-platform).
global_cases.failure_modes: AI job matching accuracy: 55% of AI recommendations not suitable for applicant (skills mismatch). Rural employment centre staff adoption required 18-month training programme. Informal economy workers (40% of labour force) not captured by platform. Matching algorithm biased toward Almaty/Nur-Sultan due to data concentration.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Enbek architecture documented in Central Asian labour market reports. KOICA actively references Enbek for UZ labour market advisory. Russian-language interface directly applicable to UZ and KG.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ Ministry of Labour is actively developing a digital employment platform. Enbek is the direct reference. UZ has 5M+ working-age unemployed/underemployed — the AI job matching and training voucher system is a PRESIDENTIAL PRIORITY (youth employment is a key political stability concern). Budget: $8-15M for UZ Enbek-equivalent. KOICA is already co-funding UZ labour market digital advisory. This is one of the strongest cases in the Labor batch.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has 600,000 registered unemployed + significant seasonal labour migration to Russia/Kazakhstan. Enbek at KG scale ($4-6M) would enable digital social contract for unemployed, training voucher management, and remittance tracking. Integration with MFSD (Ministry of Finance and Social Development) for social payment integration. KOICA KG labour advisory is active.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language interface. Adaptation for UZ/KG informal economy workers (agricultural day labour, small traders). Regional employer database building (Enbek was Almaty-centric initially — UZ/KG need oblasts/oblasts from Day 1). Labour migration module for KG (tracking circular migration to Russia/KZ).

global_cases.case_name: India e-Shram National Database of Unorganised Workers
global_cases.problem_solved: India has 400M+ unorganised/informal workers (construction, agriculture, domestic work, gig economy) without any formal employment registration, social security, or government data visibility. COVID exposed this gap — government couldn't identify or reach informal workers for relief payments. e-Shram created a universal registration system for informal workers, providing a digital identity for the unorganised sector.
global_cases.architecture_summary: National portal + Aadhaar-linked registration: informal worker self-registers with phone number + Aadhaar + trade/occupation. Universal Account Number (UAN) issued. Database linked to: PMSBY (accident insurance, ₹2 lakh auto-enrolled), PMJJBY (life insurance), construction worker welfare fund portals, state-level welfare schemes. AI analytics: occupation demand forecasting, migration pattern analysis (workers registering from different states), skill gap identification for government training programmes. Integration with EPFO for formalization tracking.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 290M+ registered workers by 2023. Occupation coverage: 400+ categories. Auto-insurance: 200M+ workers auto-enrolled in accident insurance. COVID relief: ₹500/month distributed to 29M e-Shram workers. Data use: ILO, World Bank cite as most comprehensive informal worker database globally. Worker grievance portal: 2M+ complaints filed and tracked.
global_cases.failure_modes: Data quality: 30% of entries had incorrect occupation or location data. Aadhaar exclusion: workers without Aadhaar (migrants, tribal populations) cannot register. The database registers workers but doesn't mandate employer contribution — social security gap remains. Digital literacy barrier: many construction workers needed help from mates to register.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Architecture is replicable for any country with national ID system. DPI-based registration (ID + self-reported trade). Directly applicable to UZ mahalla-level worker registration and KG's large informal labour sector.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has 5M+ informal workers (agriculture, construction, trade). No government data on this workforce. Mahalla system provides the PHYSICAL REGISTRATION NETWORK — e-Shram registration at mahalla offices is feasible. UZ digital social protection reform (World Bank DRM TA) includes informal worker tracking. Budget: $4-7M for UZ informal worker registry (using MyID as identity anchor). ILO and World Bank social protection projects as donors.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has massive informal sector (50-60% of employment). Circular migration to Russia creates data gaps. e-Shram equivalent for KG would enable: social transfer targeting, disaster relief distribution, and labour market analytics. GRS biometric ID as identity anchor. Budget: $2-4M. ILO KG programme, World Bank social protection project.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language registration. Adaptation for mahalla-based KG ayil aymak offline registration for digital-excluded workers. Avoid mandatory Aadhaar-equivalent — allow alternative ID to reach marginalized populations. Employer contribution mandate (politically harder but essential for social security).

ILO — India e-Shram Analysis

global_cases.case_name: Kazakhstan Digital Labour Migration Monitoring System
global_cases.problem_solved: Kazakhstan receives 500,000+ labour migrants annually (primarily from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan) and has 1M+ Kazakhstani workers in Russia. Manual migration tracking through border control stamps and employer work permit applications was inefficient, allowed illegal employment, and produced 6-month-delayed labour market statistics. Digital tracking would enable real-time labour migration analytics and compliant work permit management.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Integrated migration information system: border crossing data (CAMS) linked to work permit registry (Ministry of Labour), employer digital notification of migrant hiring (obligatory within 48 hours via eGov), social insurance contribution tracking for migrants (ENBEK + ENOF integration). AI module: migration flow prediction (seasonal patterns from border data + economic indicators), fake document detection (comparison of submitted work documents against national databases). Mobile app for migrants: digital work permit check + employer rating + complaint mechanism.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Registered foreign workers: 450,000 by 2022 (up from 150,000 estimated under manual system). Employer compliance rate: 78% registering migrant workers within 48 hours. Social insurance contributions from migrants: KZT 35B collected (previously near-zero). Migration flow prediction MAPE: 12% for 3-month ahead forecasts. Fake permit detection: 8,000 cases identified.
global_cases.failure_modes: Undocumented migration still significant — digital system only captures compliant employers. App adoption by migrants: 25% (language barrier for non-Russian speaking migrants, limited smartphone penetration among agricultural workers). Integration with receiving countries (UZ, KG) for bilateral data sharing: limited — one-way information flow only.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Architecture is directly applicable to UZ and KG as both source and destination countries. IOM has shared methodology. Russian-language interface is directly applicable to both countries.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has 2M+ citizens working abroad (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkey, UAE). Digital work permit system + bilateral data sharing with KZ reduces exploitation of UZ workers. For inbound migration: UZ receives Kyrgyz and Afghan agricultural workers (informal). Digital employment registration for foreign workers in UZ improves tax collection and labour rights. Budget: $5-8M. IOM and ILO are active UZ partners.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG has the most critical need: 800,000 KG citizens (12% of population) work in Russia. Bilateral KZ-KG data sharing on KG workers in KZ is already partially established. KG digital migration tracking from the source country side would enable: remittance tracking, skills mapping of returning migrants, social transfer continuity during migration. Budget: $3-5M. IOM KG programme active. This is the MOST IMPORTANT Labor case for KG.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Kyrgyz language migration worker app. Bilateral data sharing protocol with Russia (EAEU migration data framework exists). Integration with NBKR remittance data for comprehensive circular migration tracking. Protection mechanisms: migrant complaint portal with consular routing.

global_cases.case_name: Poland mObywatel App (Soviet-Bloc Evolution Reference)
global_cases.problem_solved: Poland, like UZ and KG, has a post-Soviet administrative legacy. Citizens needed to carry physical documents for employment verification, benefits access, vehicle registration, and border crossing. mObywatel (my citizen) app digitised all personal documents into a single mobile app — most relevantly for labour migration: digital employment authorization for foreign workers in Poland.
global_cases.architecture_summary: Ministry of Digital Affairs Poland: mObywatel mobile app providing: digital ID document (legally equivalent to physical ID), digital driving licence, vehicle registration card, vaccination certificate, employment authorization for foreign workers (Ukrainians, Belarusians). NFC chip reading from biometric card. Backend: national eID infrastructure (profil zaufany + eID). Work authorization: digital visa and work permit replacement, employer verification API. COVID additions: digital quarantine notice, isolation certificate. Deep Poland-Ukraine cooperation: Ukrainian Diia documents accepted by Polish mObywatel verification.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: 12M+ registered users (Poland pop 38M, high adoption). Digital work authorization: 1.5M Ukrainian workers registered in Poland via mObywatel system during 2022 crisis. Digital driving licence: 85% adoption among registered users. App satisfaction: 4.7/5. Cross-border recognition: EU member states accept mObywatel digital documents for travel.
global_cases.failure_modes: NFC reading reliability varies by phone model (older Android phones have poor NFC). Some documents not yet digitalised (gun licence, veterinary certificates). EU cross-border acceptance took 3 years of legal harmonisation.
global_cases.replicability_factors: Post-Soviet administrative evolution reference highly applicable to UZ and KG. Digital employment authorization architecture is directly relevant to UZ/KG managing their diaspora worker status. Poland-Ukraine cooperation model for UZ-KZ bilateral worker document sharing.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: mObywatel employment authorization module is directly applicable to managing UZ workers in KZ/Russia (bilateral digital permit system). UZ MyID + digital employment permit is achievable by extending existing mobile app. Key lesson: start with high-demand documents (ID + driver's licence + vehicle registration) before adding all documents. Budget: $3-5M within existing MyID programme.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG workers in Russia (800,000) would benefit enormously from digital work permit that Russian employers can verify via API. EAEU has provision for digital labour documents — KG should leverage mObywatel architecture to build compliant digital employment document for EAEU market. Budget: $2-4M.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language app. EAEU-compliant digital document standard (shared with KZ, Russia). NFC reliability on lower-end Android phones (dominant in CA). Work permit API for employers in Russia/KZ to verify KG/UZ worker documents digitally.

global_cases.case_name: UAE MoHRE AI Labour Inspection System
global_cases.problem_solved: UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) needed to modernise labour inspection for 3.8M+ migrant workers. Manual inspection visited 10% of worksites annually — inadequate for detecting wage theft, unsafe conditions, and contract fraud. AI risk scoring of workplaces could target inspections on highest-risk employers while reducing compliance burden on compliant employers.
global_cases.architecture_summary: AI Labour Inspection System: risk scoring model for 300,000+ registered employers using: wage payment patterns (via WPS — Wages Protection System electronic payroll monitoring), worker complaint data, inspection history, industry risk profile, nationality composition, turnover rate. High-risk employers flagged for inspection; low-risk employers extended to biennial inspection cycle. AI chatbot for worker complaints: 5 languages (Arabic, English, Hindi, Urdu, Filipino), available 24/7. Predictive analytics: heat-related illness risk scoring by outdoor employer type during summer months.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Inspection targeting accuracy: 75% of high-risk flagged employers had violations (vs 35% random inspection). Worker complaint resolution time: 45% reduction. Wage theft cases identified via WPS anomaly detection: 15,000 cases/year. Heat illness prevention: 55% reduction in outdoor heat illness cases in inspected high-risk sector. MoHRE awarded ILO award for labour tech innovation 2023.
global_cases.failure_modes: AI risk scoring language bias: model underweighted complaints in South Asian languages (training data dominated by Arabic/English). Some small employers categorised as high-risk due to industry type alone — regardless of actual compliance. Worker app adoption: 40% of workers prefer embassy contact to AI chatbot.
global_cases.replicability_factors: WPS (wage payment system) architecture is replicable — requires central bank payment monitoring capability. AI labour inspection risk scoring is directly applicable to CA markets where labour inspection is documented as ineffective.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has large construction, agriculture, and textile sectors with documented labour violations. MoHRE-equivalent AI labour inspection targeting would improve enforcement efficiency. UZ has a payroll reporting system (GNK) that could serve as WPS-equivalent. Budget: $5-8M for AI labour inspection platform. ILO, World Bank social protection projects as donors. Key lesson: worker complaint multilingual chatbot must work in Uzbek, Russian, and relevant migrant worker languages.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG labour inspection has very limited resources. AI risk scoring to focus limited inspectors on highest-risk employers is high-value. KG's construction and mining sectors have documented safety violations. Budget: $2-4M. ILO KG programme is the donor pathway.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz multilingual complaint chatbot. Payroll monitoring system as prerequisite (KG doesn't have WPS-equivalent — needs GNS tax data as proxy). Outdoor heat illness risk model adapted for KG (relevant for summer construction work). Labour inspector mobile app for offline field inspections.

global_cases.case_name: Bangladesh BOESL Digital Labour Export Management
global_cases.problem_solved: Bangladesh sends 700,000+ workers/year to Gulf states, Malaysia, and South Korea — but the process was dominated by unregulated manpower agents who charged illegal fees, falsified contracts, and abandoned workers. BOESL (Bureau of Overseas Employment and Training) needed digital tools to verify contracts, enable direct government-to-government worker placement, and track worker welfare post-arrival.
global_cases.architecture_summary: BOESL online platform: employer verification (foreign employers register with Bangladeshi missions abroad, verified via bilateral G2G agreements), worker application system linked to National ID (NID), digital employment contract with QR verification (prevents alteration), pre-departure briefing system (online modules), post-arrival welfare tracking (worker check-ins via app), complaint portal with embassy routing. AI component: contract fraud detection (ML on contract clauses identifying illegal terms like excessive work hours or unpaid overtime clauses), employer blacklist scoring. Smart Card for workers: NFC card with all employment details readable by Bangladesh missions.
global_cases.outcome_metrics: Illegal recruitment fee cases: 35% reduction. G2G placements: 80,000+ workers/year via verified channels (vs 0 in 2015). Contract fraud detection: 12,000 altered contracts identified. Worker welfare check-ins: 200,000+ workers tracked post-arrival. South Korea EPS (Employment Permit System) integration: 50,000 BD workers placed via digital channel.
global_cases.failure_modes: App adoption by workers in remote Bangladesh areas: 30% (digital literacy barrier). Employer blacklist enforcement: blacklisted employers register under new entity names. Post-arrival tracking voluntary — compliance falls after 3 months. Contract clause AI false positive rate: 25% for industry-standard clauses flagged as unusual.
global_cases.replicability_factors: BOESL digital platform case documented by IOM and World Bank. Directly applicable to UZ and KG which have 2-3M workers abroad in similar precarious situations. G2G labour agreement model (KZ-KG, KZ-UZ, UZ-Korea) is the policy framework needed for digital systems to work.
global_cases.uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has 2M+ migrant workers (Russia, KZ, Turkey, UAE) with documented exploitation. UZ BOESL-equivalent (Agentstvo po vneshnei trudovoi migratsii) needs digital platform for contract verification and worker welfare tracking. The KOICA-UZ Korea EPS labour programme is the immediate deployment context. Budget: $4-6M. IOM, ILO, KOICA are donors. Korea EPS integration is highest ROI application.
global_cases.kg_transferability_rationale: KG BOESL-equivalent: DODF (Department of Overseas Development and Foreign Investment). 800,000 KG workers in Russia — digital contract verification and post-arrival welfare check would address documented exploitation. G2G model with Russia (via EAEU labour protocol) and South Korea (KG-Korea EPS exists). Budget: $2-4M. IOM, KOICA KG programme.
global_cases.key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language interface. EAEU-compliant digital employment contract standard. Integration with receiving country employer verification systems (Russia: EMIAS, Korea: EPS). Worker app offline capability for use after arrival in destination country. Embassy complaint routing in destination countries.
